sculptures.name: Sri Kanyaka Parameshwari
sculptures.summary: A standing goddess framed by a flowing prabhavali arch.
sculptures.description: The goddess stands in serene frontal posture beneath a foliate prabhavali crowned with a kirtimukha. A parrot rests on the lotus in her upper hand, while finely carved girdles, bells and pleated drapery fall in layered rhythm to the lotus pedestal.

image.alt: Black stone sculpture of Sri Kanyaka Parameshwari standing under a carved arch

sculptures.name: Anantha Narayana
sculptures.summary: Vishnu seated in royal ease beneath the five-hooded Adishesha.
sculptures.description: Seated on the coils of Adishesha, Vishnu holds the chakra and shankha aloft while the serpent's five hoods open like a canopy above his crown. The granular stone gives the coils a living texture, contrasted with smooth limbs and crisp ornament.

image.alt: Grey stone sculpture of Vishnu seated beneath the five-hooded serpent Adishesha

sculptures.name: Varaha Avatar
sculptures.summary: The boar avatar of Vishnu, carved in deep relief against a temple niche.
sculptures.description: Varaha strides forward with mace in hand, a garland sweeping across his body, the small seated figure of Bhudevi resting at his shoulder. The niche behind is worked with lotus petals and scrolling vines in the temple idiom.

image.alt: Dark stone relief sculpture of Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu

sculptures.name: Radha Krishna beneath the Kadamba
sculptures.summary: An openwork panel where flute, foliage and birds intertwine.
sculptures.description: Krishna plays the flute as Radha leans in with a water pot, both standing on a double lotus base. Above them the kadamba tree dissolves into pierced, scrolling foliage alive with birds, a demanding feat of undercutting in a single panel.

image.alt: Hand-carved red wood panel of Radha and Krishna beneath an openwork tree

sculptures.name: Hoysala-style Venugopala
sculptures.summary: Krishna with the flute, framed by scenes in the Hoysala manner.
sculptures.description: Carved in the spirit of Hoysala temple art, Venugopala plays beneath a serpent-hood arch while bands of cowherds and cattle unfold on either side. The polished surface catches light along the crown, bangles and cascading jewellery.

image.alt: Hand-carved Hoysala style Krishna playing the flute

sculptures.name: Seated Radha Krishna
sculptures.summary: A tender, life-like pair captured in the carving workshop.
sculptures.description: Krishna and Radha sit side by side, he lost in the flute and she cradling a pot, their gazes turned in quiet companionship. Photographed in the workshop, it shows the soft modelling of limbs and the carved borders of their garments.

image.alt: Seated stone sculpture of Radha and Krishna in the workshop

sculptures.name: Panchamukha Ganapati
sculptures.summary: Five faces of Ganapati within a grand ornamental arch.
sculptures.description: Five elephant faces rise in a single crowned row, set inside a deep oval prabhavali of scrolling foliage with a latticed screen behind. A monumental piece whose depth of carving rewards close viewing.

image.alt: Black sculpture of five-faced Panchamukha Ganapati inside a carved arch

sculptures.name: Sri Venkateswara
sculptures.summary: The Lord of the Seven Hills, garlanded and standing tall.
sculptures.description: Venkateswara stands in benediction with the chakra and shankha raised, a long carved garland of blossoms falling to his feet. The high crown, namam and layered pedestal follow the familiar Tirumala iconography.

image.alt: Dark finish sculpture of Sri Venkateswara with a carved garland

sculptures.name: Venugopala with Prabhavali
sculptures.summary: Dancing Krishna framed by pillars and a pierced arch.
sculptures.description: Krishna dances with the flute within a pillared prabhavali, every surface worked with fine floral carving.

image.alt: Red wood sculpture of Krishna with flute in a carved arch

sculptures.name: Nritya Ganapati
sculptures.summary: Ganapati in joyous dance on a lotus pedestal.
sculptures.description: A free-standing dancing Ganapati, the raised leg and swaying arms carved with a lively sense of movement.

image.alt: Red wood sculpture of dancing Ganapati

sculptures.name: Krishna in Openwork Arch
sculptures.summary: A flute-playing Krishna enveloped in lace-like carving.
sculptures.description: Krishna stands within a dense openwork surround of foliage and figures, a showcase of pierced woodcarving.

image.alt: Red wood openwork carving of Krishna playing the flute

sculptures.name: Seated Ganapati
sculptures.summary: Ganapati enthroned beneath a kirtimukha arch.
sculptures.description: A seated Ganapati in classical posture, framed by pillars and a kirtimukha-crowned arch.

image.alt: Grey stone sculpture of seated Ganapati

sculptures.name: Seated Lakshmi
sculptures.summary: The goddess of abundance seated in grace.
sculptures.description: Four-armed Lakshmi sits in a relaxed pose under a scrolling arch, an elephant motif carved into the base.

image.alt: Grey stone sculpture of seated Lakshmi

sculptures.name: Radha Krishna with Kamadhenu
sculptures.summary: The divine couple with the sacred cow, cast in gleaming brass.
sculptures.description: Radha and Krishna stand together with the flute, the sacred cow at their side, in a polished brass casting.

image.alt: Brass sculpture of Radha and Krishna with a cow

sculptures.name: Seated Shiva
sculptures.summary: Shiva with trishula and damaru, seated on the rock of Kailasa.
sculptures.description: Four-armed Shiva sits in benediction, holding the trishula and damaru, with crescent moon and flowing locks.

image.alt: Brass sculpture of seated Shiva with trishula

sculptures.name: Kneeling Hanuman
sculptures.summary: Hanuman in devoted salute with his mace.
sculptures.description: Hanuman kneels with one hand raised in blessing and the gada resting on his shoulder, on an ornamented oval base.

image.alt: Brass sculpture of kneeling Hanuman holding a mace

sculptures.name: Standing Vishnu in Marble
sculptures.summary: Vishnu in benediction, his marble form touched with gold.
sculptures.description: A standing four-armed Vishnu beneath an arched frame, the white marble heightened with gilding on the crown, garments and attributes, with a small devotee at his side.

image.alt: White marble sculpture of standing Vishnu with gilded details

sculptures.name: Goddess Sarasvati
sculptures.summary: The goddess of wisdom in graceful tribhanga, finely jewelled.
sculptures.description: Sarasvati stands in a gentle three-bend posture holding a manuscript and water vessel, her jewellery and halo carved with remarkable delicacy, attended by small figures at her feet.

image.alt: Marble sculpture of the goddess Sarasvati standing with attendants

sculptures.name: Celestial Nymph Bracket
sculptures.summary: A temple bracket alive with movement and playful grace.
sculptures.description: Carved as an architectural bracket, a celestial nymph turns in a lively pose, teasing a boy at her side. The deep undercutting lets light pass through the marble.

image.alt: Marble temple bracket carved as a celestial nymph

reference.credit: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

sculptures.name: Jina Neminatha
sculptures.summary: A meditating Jina enthroned beneath an ornate canopy.
sculptures.description: The Jina sits in deep meditation on a lion throne, framed by a canopy of elephants, foliage and attendant figures, with Ambika and Gomedha carved at the base.

image.alt: Marble sculpture of the seated Jina Neminatha under a carved canopy

sculptures.name: Saraswati with Tirthankaras
sculptures.summary: The goddess framed by a lace-like marble shrine.
sculptures.description: Saraswati stands within a richly pierced frame filled with tirthankaras, celestial beings and donors, a showcase of the fine detail marble allows.

image.alt: Marble sculpture of Saraswati within a carved frame of small figures

categories.name: Stone Sculptures
categories.description: Hand-sculpted stone statues created by skilled artisans with timeless craftsmanship: strong, elegant and made for a lifetime of worship.

categories.name: Wood Sculptures
categories.description: Divine wooden statues with detailed hand-carving and traditional artistry, with a natural finish and lasting quality in every piece.

categories.name: Metal Sculptures
categories.tagline: Crafted to inspire. Built to last.
categories.description: Moulded metal statues made with precision, shine and durability, suited to temples, homes and meaningful gifting.

categories.name: Marble Sculptures
categories.description: Sculptures in fine white marble, prized for its soft translucence and the delicate detail it can hold, from serene deities to ornamental pieces.

site.name: Devalok Sculptures
site.description: Devalok Sculptures brings devotion to life through finely crafted stone, wood, metal and marble sculptures that celebrate India's timeless spiritual heritage.
site.vision: To preserve India's spiritual artistry by creating timeless sculptures.
site.mission: To craft authentic stone, metal, and wood sculptures through skilled artisans.

values.title: Artistry
values.text: Every form begins as a drawing of proportion and posture, refined until the figure feels alive in its stillness.

values.title: Craftsmanship
values.text: Stone, wood, metal and marble are shaped by skilled hands, with the patience each material asks for.

values.title: Cultural Inspiration
values.text: Our forms draw on India's temple traditions, from the ornate prabhavali arch to the grace of a dancing Ganapati.

values.title: Attention to Detail
values.text: Crowns, jewellery, drapery and lotus bases are carved line by line, because devotion lives in the details.
